name: Yokohama Pidgin
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only known documentation is Atkinson 1879 humorous phrasebook 'Exercises in the Yokohama Dialect'; no stress description located

sources.citation: Avram, Andrei A. 2017. "Two sides of the same coin": Yokohama Pidgin Japanese and Japanese Pidgin English. Acta Linguistica Asiatica 7(1): 57-76. DOI 10.4312/ala.7.1.57-76.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2 'Phonology' repeats the segmental and syllable-structure points of Avram 2014; no stress/accent terms occur.

sources.citation: Avram, Andrei A. 2014. Yokohama Pidgin Japanese revisited. Acta Linguistica Asiatica 4(2): 67-84. DOI 10.4312/ala.4.2.67-84.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 'Phonology' (pp. 70-72) covers high-vowel devoicing/deletion, [ʃ] for [ç], word-internal [ŋ], Japanese-type syllable structure with /N/ as only coda, loanword epenthesis/paragoge, inter-speaker variation; no mention of stress, accent, pitch or prosody. Author notes phonological interpretation of the written records 'can only be rather tentative'.

sources.citation: Chamberlain, Basil Hall. 1904. Things Japanese, 4th ed. London: Murray. Entry 'Pidgin-Japanese', pp. 365-366. (archive.org 4ththingsjapanes00chamuoft)
sources.note: Nothing; anecdotal entry with a few lexical examples.

sources.citation: Anon. 1879. A new dialect; or, Yokohama Pidgin. Littell's Living Age 142 (no. 1836): 496-500; Diósy, A. 1879. Japoniana curiosissima. ibid. 500-501. (archive.org sim_living-age_1879-08-23_142_1836)
sources.note: Nothing; review of Atkinson with word lists and etymologies, one note on Chinese pronunciation of r.

sources.citation: Atkinson, Hoffman ['Bishop of Homoco']. 1879. Revised and enlarged edition of Exercises in the Yokohama Dialect. Yokohama: Japan Gazette Office. (archive.org revisedenlargede00atki)
sources.note: Nothing. Humorous phrasebook in English-based respelling; the only pronunciation remark concerns r as rendered by Westerners vs. Chinese (pp. 28-29).

sources.citation: Inoue, Aya. 2006. Grammatical features of Yokohama Pidgin Japanese: Common characteristics of restricted pidgins. Japanese/Korean Linguistics 15: 55-66. Stanford: CSLI.

sources.note: Only other linguistically trained treatment of YPJ (Daniels was a Japanese phonetician at SOAS); Avram cites it for pronunciation remarks (pp. 810, 813); if any source comments on accent in the ports lingo it would be this one, though it is primarily lexical.
